strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local compute (vector projection and scaling) between each. Requires 8 all-reduce dispatches on tensors of size 16384. Represents the reference implementation with no fusion or overlap—highest dispatch count but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused Scalar Reduction with Vector Broadcast
strategies.desc: Splits the problem into alternating vector all-reduce (for s) and scalar all-reduce (for the mean projection term v·s). By computing the mean locally first, then all-reducing the scalar, we can reduce payload size for half the operations. Requires 8 vector + 8 scalar all-reduces (16 dispatches total) but with smaller total bytes transferred due to scalar reductions.

strategies.name: Concatenated Dual-Channel All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Concatenates [s, projection_term] into a single tensor and performs one all-reduce per iteration, recovering both the sum and the projection statistics in one collective. Requires 8 all-reduce dispatches on tensors of size 16385 (16384 + 1 scalar). Trades slightly larger payload for eliminating half the dispatch overhead compared to strategy 2.

strategies.name: Pipelined Two-Stage Batched Collectives
strategies.desc: Groups the 8 iterations into 2 batches of 4, stacking intermediate results into a single [4, 16384] tensor and issuing batch all-reduces. Uses reduce-scatter followed by all-gather within each batch to pipeline computation and communication. Requires ~4-6 dispatches total depending on batch strategy, trading increased local memory and complexity for fewer collectives.

strategies.name: Algebraic Rewrite with Single Final All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Analytically composes the 8 dependent iterations into a closed-form expression by tracking the linear transformation applied at each step, then performs a single all-reduce on a modified initial payload that encodes all iteration state. Requires 1-2 all-reduce dispatches but with significantly more complex local preprocessing and postprocessing arithmetic to construct and decode the transformed representation.
